title: AI music maker Suno now generates spoken words
slides: Suno just learned to speak. Can it replace voice actors?
The AI music tool now generates spoken word audio too
But the voice synthesis lacks emotional nuance of humans
Podcasters can draft full episodes without recording anything
Test one voiceover today: does it pass your ear?
thread_text:
1. Voice Actors at Risk

Suno now generates spoken-word audio, letting anyone produce broadcast-quality voiceovers without a microphone or a human voice actor.

2. Podcast Without Recording

Creators can draft entire episodes using Suno's new text-to-speech feature, skipping the recording studio and editing time.

3. Emotion Missing

The output sounds flat compared to human delivery. Suno's synthetic voice lacks the emotional nuance that trained actors bring to scripts.

4. The Real Trade-Off

Speed and cost savings come at a price. If you have to re-edit to inject feeling, have you really saved time?

5. Test Your Own Ear

Generate one voiceover with Suno today and play it for a colleague. Ask them: does this pass as human, or does it give itself away?

instagram.caption:
Need a voiceover for a podcast episode? You can now generate it without recording a single word.

Suno, previously known for making music, now produces spoken-word audio too. 🎙️ Anyone can draft a full episode without a microphone or a voice actor.

The catch: the output sounds flat. It lacks the emotional nuance a trained human brings. 😕

For creators, that means speed and cost savings — but also re-edits if you want feeling in the delivery.

Generate one voiceover with Suno today and play it for someone. Ask: does it pass as human? 🤔
